seoTitle: Cannes cruise port guide: tenders, Le Suquet, Lérins islands
seoDescription: Cannes is a tender port: boats land at the Vieux Port, a short walk from La Croisette. Lérins ferry €18.50–€19 (2026), city bus €1.50, station 10 min on foot.
quickAnswer: Cannes is a tender port: ships anchor in the bay and tenders land at the Vieux Port, a short walk from the Palais des Festivals, La Croisette and Le Suquet. The station is about 10 minutes on foot, and ferries to Île Sainte-Marguerite leave from the same harbour. Be back at the tender landing 90 minutes before all-aboard, and 120 minutes before if your day includes a train.
intro: Cannes has no quay for large cruise ships, so they anchor in the bay and passengers come ashore by tender to the Vieux Port, a short walk from the Palais des Festivals. From 2026 the city caps cruise passengers landing at 6,000 a day and allows one large ship a day, never two at once; calls by large ships were set to fall from 175 in 2024 to 34 in 2026. Everything in the centre is on foot from the landing: the old quarter of Le Suquet above the harbour, the Forville market and La Croisette. The Lérins islands are a short ferry ride away.
tenderNotes: Ships anchor in the bay and tenders land at the Vieux Port, beside the city centre. The ride takes about 10–15 minutes depending on the sea. There are toilets by the tender dock. Afternoon queues can build, so allow extra time for the ride back.

terminals.name: Vieux Port tender landing
terminals.notes: The tender dock is within walking distance of shops, restaurants and Le Suquet. The tourist office is in the Palais des Festivals building at 1 Boulevard de la Croisette, about five blocks from the dock. The train station is about 700 m away, roughly 10 minutes on foot. Ferries to the Lérins islands leave from the same harbour.

walkability.detail: The centre and beaches are about 5–10 minutes from the tender landing and the station about 10 minutes. Le Suquet is a short climb up from the harbour.

transportSections.time: 5–10 min to the centre and beaches; about 10 min to the station
transportSections.detail: Walk from the Vieux Port to the Palais des Festivals and along La Croisette, or up to Le Suquet. Most of what a cruise visitor wants is within this area.

transportSections.time: About 15 minutes; about one crossing an hour in the day
transportSections.detail: Two operators run from the Vieux Port. Riviera Lines lists departures from Cannes at 09:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00, 14:00, 15:00 and 16:00, with returns at 10:15, 11:15, 12:15, 14:15, 15:15, 16:15 and 17:00; it notes that times are not guaranteed, so confirm when you buy. Check whether your ticket is a return.

transportSections.cost: €1.50 single, €12.50 for 10 journeys (2026); Suquet–Forville shuttle pass €1.50
transportSections.time: City Palm every 10–15 minutes, Monday to Saturday, 09:00–19:15
transportSections.detail: The City Palm shuttle links the town hall, La Croisette, Rue d'Antibes and the station. A separate shuttle runs from the town hall up to Le Suquet every 25 minutes from 09:00 to 19:00, useful if you want to avoid the climb.

transportSections.cost: Fare not confirmed for this guide; check SNCF TER before you travel
transportSections.time: Nice about 30–40 min; Monaco about 1 hour
transportSections.detail: Walk about 10 minutes from the tender landing to Cannes station. Trains run frequently. Monaco is a long round trip on a tender day; leave plenty of margin.
Taxis are usually available near the harbour. Convenient for short hops, but expensive for longer trips.

returnTiming.rule: Be back at the tender landing at the Vieux Port 90 minutes before all-aboard if you stay in Cannes or go to Île Sainte-Marguerite. If your day includes a train to Nice or Monaco, be back at the landing 120 minutes before all-aboard.
returnTiming.detail: Tender queues build in the afternoon. From Île Sainte-Marguerite, take a ferry that leaves the island at least 105 minutes before all-aboard; with about one boat an hour, check the return times when you buy. From Nice-Ville, take a train that leaves at least 170 minutes before all-aboard; from Monaco, at least 190 minutes before.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If a train is delayed, take a taxi from Cannes station to the Vieux Port. If you will miss the last tender, call the port agent number on your daily programme at once.

excursionAdvice: Cannes itself and Île Sainte-Marguerite are easy on your own, so neither needs a tour. A ship tour makes sense for Monaco, which is about an hour each way by train, and for the hill villages inland, where public transport is hard to time around tenders.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship anchors at 08:00, tenders start soon after, and all-aboard is 17:30.

steps.what: Tender ashore to the Vieux Port and walk up to Le Suquet.
Walk down to the Forville market, open Tuesday to Sunday mornings.
Take a ferry from the Vieux Port to Île Sainte-Marguerite.
Visit Fort Royal and the Musée du Masque de Fer, then walk the island paths.
Picnic or lunch on the island.
Walk along La Croisette past the Palais des Festivals.
At the tender landing, 90 minutes before all-aboard because the ship is at anchor.

sights.name: Le Suquet
sights.why: The old quarter on the hill above the Vieux Port, with cafés and the Musée des Explorations du Monde at the top.
sights.tip: The Suquet shuttle from the town hall runs every 25 minutes, 09:00–19:00, if you want to skip the climb.

sights.name: Musée des Explorations du Monde
sights.why: Museum at the top of Le Suquet with Mediterranean antiquities, world musical instruments, tribal arts and paintings including Artemisia Gentileschi's Judith and Holofernes.
sights.tip: Closed for works from 14 September to 30 October 2026, and on Mondays outside July and August. From November to March it opens 10:00–13:00 and 14:00–17:00.

sights.name: Île Sainte-Marguerite and Fort Royal
sights.why: The larger Lérins island, about 15 minutes by ferry, with the Fort Royal.
sights.tip: Check the return ferry times when you buy; boats run about once an hour.

sights.name: Musée du Masque de Fer
sights.why: Museum in Fort Royal with the cell said to have held the Man in the Iron Mask, Roman cisterns and finds from two shipwrecks.
sights.tip: June to September open daily 10:30–17:45; October to March closed Mondays and open 10:30–13:15 and 14:15–16:45.

sights.name: La Croisette
sights.why: The seafront boulevard of hotels, beaches and the Palais des Festivals.
sights.tip: Start at the Palais des Festivals, where the tourist office is.

sights.name: Marché Forville
sights.why: Covered market in a 1930s building near the Vieux Port.
sights.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday mornings only.

sights.name: Petit train tours
sights.why: Two motorised tours of about 35 minutes each, one through Le Suquet and one along La Croisette and Rue d'Antibes.
sights.tip: They leave from the seaward side of the Palais des Festivals in the morning.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving the return to the last tender.
commonMistakes.fix: Afternoon queues build at the Vieux Port. Be at the landing 90 minutes before all-aboard, or 120 if you went to Nice or Monaco.

commonMistakes.mistake: Missing the last useful ferry back from Île Sainte-Marguerite.
commonMistakes.fix: Boats run about once an hour. Note the return times when you buy and take one that leaves at least 105 minutes before all-aboard.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning Monaco on a tender day without a margin.
commonMistakes.fix: It is about an hour each way by train. Leave Monaco at least 190 minutes before all-aboard, or take the ship tour.

commonMistakes.mistake: Heading for the Musée des Explorations du Monde on a Monday or during works.
commonMistakes.fix: It is closed on Mondays outside July and August, and closed for works from 14 September to 30 October 2026.

commonMistakes.mistake: Arriving at the Forville market in the afternoon.
commonMistakes.fix: It trades on Tuesday to Sunday mornings only.

safety: Cannes centre is busy and generally safe on foot. The UK Foreign Office warns that pickpockets in France work in gangs, with one distracting you while another goes into your bag, and that thieves work at stations and around tourist sights and cash machines. Carry your bag across your body and keep cards and passport apart. Tender transfers can be suspended in rough seas, so check the ship's announcements before going far.
scams: Distraction thefts by pickpocket teams at stations and around tourist sights, where one person distracts you while another takes from your bag.
accessibility: Tender transfers depend on sea state; wheelchair users should check with the ship on the day. The Palais des Festivals and La Croisette are a short walk from the landing. Le Suquet is a climb, but the Suquet shuttle bus from the town hall avoids it.
rainyDay: Visit the Musée des Explorations du Monde when it is open, browse the covered Forville market in the morning, or take the ferry to the Musée du Masque de Fer on Île Sainte-Marguerite. Ferries and tenders may stop in rough weather, so stay near the Vieux Port if the sea is up.
crowdTips: From 2026 Cannes caps cruise passengers landing at 6,000 a day and allows one large ship a day, so the centre is less crowded by cruise traffic than before. Go ashore early, take an early ferry to the islands, and visit the Forville market before late morning.

faqs.a: Yes. Ships anchor in the bay and tenders, about 10–15 minutes each way, land at the Vieux Port beside the city centre.

faqs.q: Is Cannes walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. The centre and beaches are about 5–10 minutes from the tender landing. Le Suquet is a short climb.

faqs.q: How do I get from Cannes cruise port to the Lérins islands?
faqs.a: Ferries to Île Sainte-Marguerite leave from the Vieux Port about once an hour and take about 15 minutes. Adult fares are €18.50 or €19.00 depending on the operator (2026).

faqs.q: How far is Cannes train station from the tender port?
faqs.a: About 700 m, roughly 10 minutes on foot.

faqs.q: Can I visit Nice or Monaco from Cannes on my own?
faqs.a: Nice is about 30–40 minutes by train and Monaco about an hour. Both are possible, but leave Nice at least 170 minutes and Monaco at least 190 minutes before all-aboard.

faqs.q: What can I do in Cannes in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Walk up to Le Suquet, visit the Forville market, take the ferry to Île Sainte-Marguerite and Fort Royal, and finish on La Croisette.
The La Croisette beaches and the Plage du Midi are both about 5–10 minutes' walk from the tender landing.
Yes. Watch for pickpockets in crowds and at the station, and allow time for the tender queue on your return.
